key_insight: The paper proposes Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI), a new paradigm that solves inverse problems by exploiting inherent mathematical or physical structure instead of relying on iterative objective minimization.
engineering_relevance: SDI could improve efficiency, interpretability, and multi-parameter decoupling in inverse-problem workflows used in imaging, PDE-based reconstruction, and scientific machine learning.
method: MSDI: use mathematical structure to build a pseudo-inverse in the spectral domain via unitary diagonalization.
PSDI: use physical structure to drive inversion through virtual-source projection (PSDWII) or physical-system analogy (PSDBP).
Positions SDI as a complement and extension to traditional optimization-driven inversion, not a replacement.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and paradigm-setting; it presents representative methods but does not report experimental metrics or benchmark results.
watch_item: The approach may depend on strong problem structure and carefully chosen spectral/physical assumptions, which could limit robustness on noisy or weakly structured inverse problems.
paper_title: Structure-Driven Inversion: A New Paradigm for Solving Inverse Problems
